title: Author removes any comment or reply at any depth: a 'comment removed' placeholder keeps visible replies in place, empty ones vanish, and public counts drop by one
how_to_read: Each attempt is one line and a `details` filename in this same directory. Open a detail file ONLY when this index points you at one -- the summaries are here so you do not have to. `caused_by` is what sent the stage back; `changed` is what the attempt then touched, counted by kind. Several attempts in a row that were caused by the same stage and changed no `src` is a loop, not progress.

open.issue: C1 (derived from 'The author can delete any comment or reply, at any depth'): the pinned owner, and only the owner, can remove any comment or reply at any depth: missing
C2 (derived from 'from the report page'): the owner has a remove control on each comment drawn on the report page and on the branch page: missing
C3 (derived from 'or admin'): the owner can remove a comment from the admin side: missing
C4 (derived from 'it disappears for everyone'): once removed, the comment's text and author are shown to nobody (anonymous, reader, owner) on /reports/<slug>, the home page or a branch page: partial

C7 (derived from 'public comment counts drop by one'): a public visible-comment count exists wherever the report is listed or shown, and after a removal it is exactly one lower. A placeholder is not counted, and the visible replies under it still are: missing

Where the code lives: the remove handler in admin.go beside adminFeedbackReply (practice, chosen) or comment.go (crossdomain); SC-021's comments-side code in comments.go (practice) or a new internal/comments/block.go (crossdomain, chosen), with Remove kept in comments.go.
Lookup naming and shape: RemoveTarget returning (slug, published, err) (practice, chosen, mirroring OwnerReplyTarget) or Locate returning a Target struct (crossdomain).
The viewer flag through buildThread: a second bool parameter (practice) or a threadViewer{SignedIn, Owner} struct (crossdomain, chosen, so two adjacent bools cannot be swapped).
The landing field: `back` with a strict 400 on other values (practice) or `from` matched leniently (crossdomain). Chosen: the name `from`, with practice's strict parse.
Admin page: a 'N comments' line in the moderation section (practice) or none (crossdomain, chosen). Item element ids: mod-<n> (crossdomain) or none (chosen).
Where the Block form appears: inside the owner's details on reader pages and on the admin list (practice), or on the admin moderation list only (crossdomain, chosen).

A blocked account's refusal: per-package existing errors (404 for comments and feedback, a new ErrRefused 403 for votes; practice) or one ErrBlocked meaning 403 everywhere through a follow-up read (crossdomain, chosen).

Blocking an id that never signed in: refused 404 through INSERT…SELECT FROM users (practice) or allowed through INSERT…VALUES ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING (crossdomain, chosen, per the migration's 'a block is a fact about an account').
All [SC-021] components (block store, blocked refusals, feedback blocked mark, block and unblock routes, the Blocked users page, Block forms). E-006 lines 1 and 2 cannot exit 0 until they land.
Case 14, a removal racing 20 concurrent Posts: the design marked it material:false.
Deferred findings m4, m5 and m7 (decided deferrals); waived m3 and m6 (O-018, O-019).

critique missed: The design's handler step 3 was 'MaxBytesReader with a 1 KiB cap, then ParseForm' for a route whose only field is optional. The critique never asked what ParseForm does with a multipart, text/plain, JSON or untyped body. It reads none of them, so the cap never trips and the absent-`from` arm removes the comment. That breaks the contract's own 'unreadable body or over 1 KiB: 400; every refusal changes nothing' on an irreversible action. A check that would have caught it: take each sibling handler's required field away and see which body shapes still reach the write.

critique missed: The critique did not check whether the design's case `check` commands could be run and judged by the engine. C-005 put '|' inside a slash `-run` pattern, which Go splits per level, so it ran only the first top-level test. Case 13's pass condition was 'exits 1', which the engine reads as a failing command. Both cases were marked owed to the build and could not be discharged as written. This forced build attempt 2 to rewrite them.

code-review missed: internal/server/admin.go lost its gofmt formatting (no blank line between the closing brace of removeFrom and the comment of adminRaw, admin.go:333). Code review #4 recorded it under LEFT OPEN as 'formatting is code, so I did not touch it' and did not file it as a finding. No review ran gofmt, and the CRLF working tree makes `gofmt -l` useless unless it is run on LF blobs. Validate caught it later.

Sent back with what raised them: O-021 (fix): M1 (major): The `because` text this build wrote for the rule 'removal never deletes a comment row' (O-016's 'named holes') is an unquoted, plain YAML scalar. It contains ': ' at line 421 ('un-remove: visibleSQL') and ends line 423 with ':' ('...a removed comment):'). YAML reads either as a mapping indicator, so a real YAML parser rejects the whole file. The engine's Fitness op=check on this tree answers `ERROR: .taad itness.yaml could not be read: ScannerError: mapping values are not allowed here in ... line 421, column 42`. So none of the project's architecture rules is evaluated by the engine any more: the privacy fences, the transaction fences, the must_not_import rules, and the two rules this slice adds. internal/fitnessrules/rules_test.go loads the file with a lenient line-by-line regexp reader (loadRules), so `go test` stays green and hides this. That reader also skips must_not_import on files that open with a doc comment (#931), so those import rules are now enforced nowhere. The base file at e64753c has no plain scalar holding ': ', a trailing ':' or ' #' (checked with the same scan: none found). The two offending lines are this build's additions. Make the `because` a single-quoted scalar, as the sibling rules' are, doubling the apostrophes in 'vanish' and SC-021's. Or reword the two spots: 'un-remove: visibleSQL' becomes 'un-remove, because visibleSQL', and 'a removed comment):' becomes 'a removed comment),'. Then re-run Fitness op=check and confirm it reads the file. CLOSE THE CLASS, NOT THIS INSTANCE. M1 is one member of "fitness.yaml text that the engine's YAML reader refuses but the lenient Go line loader accepts" (members come from ordinary input, by accident). Enumerate the class into a corpus committed with the code -- a table of inputs, fire/quiet plant rows, an alias list, a census of every type that carries the value -- in the repository or .taad/slices/SL-010/, make every row pass, and show the code before your fix failing the rows you claim to close. The engine runs `go test -count=1 -run TestFitnessYAMLPlainScalarsParse ./internal/fitnessrules/` again in your tree, and that run is what closes this; your word does not. The test: package fitnessrules import ( "os" "path/filepath" "regexp" "strings" "testing" ) // TestFitnessYAMLPlainScalarsParse checks that every unquoted (plain) YAML scalar // in .taad/fitness.yaml is one a YAML parser accepts. A plain scalar may not hold // ": " or end a line with ":" (YAML reads either as a mapping key), nor " #" (a // comment). The engine reads this file with a real YAML parser: one bad scalar // makes the whole file unreadable and no rule in it is enforced. func TestFitnessYAMLPlainScalarsParse(t *testing.T) { data, err := os.ReadFile(filepath.Join(repoRoot(t), ".taad", "fitness.yaml")) if err != nil { t.Fatal(err) } lines := strings.Split(strings.ReplaceAll(string(data), "
", "

") key := regexp.MustCompile(`^(\s*)(?:- )?([a-z_]+):\s+(.*)$`) item := regexp.MustCompile(`^\s*- `) bare := regexp.MustCompile(`^\s*[a-z_]+:(\s|$)`) indent := func(s string) int { return len(s) - len(strings.TrimLeft(s, " ")) } for i := 0; i < len(lines); { m := key.FindStringSubmatch(lines[i]) if m == nil || m[3] == "" || strings.ContainsRune(`'"|>[{&*!`, rune(m[3][0])) { i++ continue } type piece struct { n int v string } vals := []piece{{i + 1, m[3]}} j := i + 1 for j < len(lines) && strings.TrimSpace(lines[j]) != "" && indent(lines[j]) > len(m[1]) && !item.MatchString(lines[j]) && !bare.MatchString(lines[j]) { vals = append(vals, piece{j + 1, strings.TrimSpace(lines[j])}) j++ } for _, p := range vals { if strings.Contains(p.v, ": ") || strings.HasSuffix(p.v, ":") || strings.Contains(p.v, " #") { t.Errorf("fitness.yaml:%d: a plain scalar a YAML parser refuses: %q", p.n, p.v) } } i = j } }
